process.title: Discovery
process.description: We understand the business goal, the audience, the brand constraints, and the technical limits. I define scope, risks, and deliverables before choosing tools or writing a line of code.

process.title: Design, systems & architecture
process.description: I define the architecture, the content model, and the design system: tokens, components, and patterns. I prototype key screens and flows (web, CMS, and automation/AI touchpoints) to validate direction before building at scale.

process.title: Build & automation
process.description: I build in short iterations with verifiable deliveries: typed, accessible, and optimized implementations across web frameworks, CMS, and workflows (n8n, MCP, and more), deployed to previews from day one.

process.title: Delivery, handoff & ownership
process.description: Deploy to production, set up analytics and automation, and create living documentation and training so your team can keep iterating and own the system without depending on me for every change.

faq.q: How is a project measured in Essentials and Growth?
faq.a: A base project is a complete site of up to four sections (for example, a home plus 3 sections), with a maximum of 6 strips per page so a single page doesn't grow without limit. It's the unit I use to measure monthly capacity. When scope grows, it's normalized: an eight-section site counts as two base projects, even if it's a single URL, because the work equals two. Pieces with their own logic, like an online store (catalog, cart, checkout), aren't a base project; they're quoted separately or as several units depending on scope. That way "5 projects per month" means clear, measurable capacity, not an ambiguous number. Visionary, by contrast, is measured by hours of dedicated engineering, not by projects, given the variable scope of its initiatives.

faq.q: What does the Visionary package include?
a: Visionary is the technical partner tier. It includes everything in Growth and adds architecture for content platforms, editorial sites, and complex web systems; implementation in modern frameworks like Next.js, Astro, and Payload; and advanced automations, assistants, chatbots, and AI flows connected to your real operation.

It gives you the technical foundation to open premium offerings like online stores, content platforms, and brand experiences powered by AI, the capacity that usually requires an in-house technical team without having to build one. It's measured by 36 hours of dedicated engineering per month, plus a weekly studio visit and advisory meetings as extra time.

faq.q: How do meetings and studio visits work?
faq.a: Meetings and the weekly studio visit are extra time included: they don't consume your projects or Visionary's hours. Growth includes up to 4 hours of meetings per week and Visionary up to 8, plus a weekly studio visit for alignment and in-person planning. Essentials focuses on implementation, with no recurring meetings included. The intent is that strategy and alignment don't cost you delivery capacity.

faq.q: What does each retainer's scope cover?
faq.a: Each retainer is based on a capacity defined up front: base projects on Essentials and Growth, or hours on Visionary, across agreed types of work (sites, landings, CMS, automations, etc.). Any initiative outside that capacity is quoted as an additional project. It isn't «whatever comes up that month», but a fixed web engineering and design capacity used against a backlog agreed with Pigmento.

faq.q: How is a project priced?
faq.a: I start from the discovery scope. For scoped pieces I use a fixed price; for full projects I quote by scope; and for ongoing work I use a monthly retainer.

faq.q: How is the backlog prioritized?
faq.a: Requests are grouped into a monthly backlog. We prioritize together with Pigmento what goes into each cycle; whatever doesn't fit moves to the next one, or is quoted as a separate project if it needs extra urgency.

faq.q: How are responsibilities shared?
faq.a: Pigmento keeps control over brand strategy, content, and the relationship with its clients; I own the web layer, systems, and automations within the defined scope. Any major strategic change is reviewed before taking it on within the retainer.

faq.q: Are tools and licenses included?
faq.a: Use of my toolbox (Figma, Adobe, motion libs, CMS, n8n, Claude, Cursor, etc.) is included in the retainer. Specific enterprise licenses, third-party infrastructure, or accounts owned by the client are budgeted separately when needed.

faq.q: What about infrastructure and major support?
faq.a: Packages cover design, implementation, automations, and standard deploys. Major infrastructure changes (hosting migrations, full stack refactors, adopting new platforms) are framed as projects with their own scope.

faq.q: Can you join an existing team?
faq.a: Yes. I plug into your processes, repos, and tools, or I lead the web technical side end to end, whatever you need.

faq.q: What stack do you use?
a: I work with modern JS frameworks like Next.js, Astro, and React, with TypeScript and token-based design systems for UI.
For content and data I use CMSs and APIs such as Payload, Strapi, Webflow, and headless WordPress, plus workflow automation with n8n when it helps the team.
Infrastructure usually runs on Vercel and Cloudflare, with Supabase/Postgres and CI/CD where the project needs it.
On top of that, I integrate AI tooling (Claude, MCP servers, agents) to support documentation, content, and internal workflows when it adds real value.
The stack is always adapted to the project and to how much ownership your team wants over the final system, not to a single “favorite tool”.

faq.q: Do you work remotely?
faq.a: Yes. I work remotely with teams in North America, LATAM, and Europe, in time zones compatible with the Americas.

faq.q: Can you include these projects in your portfolio?
faq.a: Yes, but only as attribution, never as ownership. If I feature any of the projects I build for Pigmento Studio, I always present it as a collaboration: I credit my role in building it, without claiming the project as my own.

faq.q: How do I decide between repairing or rebuilding from scratch?
faq.a: If your priority is selling again this week and the rest of the site works fine, the repair is faster and cheaper. If you also want to leave WordPress behind and run on a managed platform, the Shopify rebuild solves both at once, at a higher cost and timeline.

faq.q: What happens to the payment gateway that already works?
faq.a: On the repair, I don't touch it: it keeps running as-is. On the Shopify rebuild, I integrate it again in full against the account you manage.

faq.q: Can I start with the repair and migrate to Shopify later?
faq.a: Yes. They're independent options: you can repair now to start selling again, and evaluate the Shopify migration later as a separate project.

faq.q: Why are there two different prices?
faq.a: Because they're two different technical routes, not a range on the same work: repairing costs less because it doesn't touch the platform; rebuilding on Shopify costs more because it's a full new site. Each price is fixed for the scope described in its option.

faq.q: How do payments work?
faq.a: A 50% deposit reserves the project on the calendar and kicks off discovery; the remaining 50% is due on delivery. Prices are tax-free.

faq.q: How long does each option take?
a: The WooCommerce repair usually wraps in 1-2 weeks, depending on how deep the problem goes.
The full Shopify rebuild takes longer: 4 to 6 weeks, depending on the catalog scope confirmed in discovery.

faq.q: Do you work remotely?
faq.a: Yes. I work remotely with teams in North America, LATAM, and Europe, in time zones compatible with the Americas.

faq.q: Can you include this project in your portfolio?
faq.a: Yes, but only as attribution, never as ownership. If I feature the project, I always present it as a collaboration: I credit my role in building it, without claiming the project as my own.
